messages:
morgan: Heads up — noticed a regression when bringing up shortvec-7B int4 on the short-query holdout. recall@1 dropped ~12ppt vs fp16 baseline, recall@10 looks mostly unchanged. digging now.

devansh: ugh. can you paste the eval command + a quick table of metric diffs?

morgan: sure — ran the usual harness: `python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm l2 --seed 42`

morgan: quick numbers (holdout = 10k queries): fp16 -> recall@1 0.68, recall@10 0.86; int4 -> recall@1 0.56, recall@10 0.84

jia: interesting that recall@10 is fine. sounds like top-1 ranking noise — maybe cosine small-angle perturbation pushing the right doc from 1 to 2-3. did you histogram cosine deltas?

morgan: yes, looked at the delta between fp16 vs int4 cosines for positive pairs. mean delta ~ -0.007 but the tail at high cosines has a few spikes ~ -0.02. rough plot attached (i'll drop in the notebook).

anya: could be quantization scaling mismatch for short vectors. short queries have fewer tokens -> smaller magnitude embeddings? check per-tensor vs per-channel quantization configs. which quant backend did you use?

morgan: used `quantize_backend=fastq` (default on the infra) and `per_channel=false`.

devansh: try rerun with `--per_channel=true` and `--aq-bias-correct=true` if the backend supports it. also try toggling `norming` — maybe fp16 had implicit postnorm differences.

morgan: running a couple quick jobs now:
```
python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --per_channel true --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm l2 --seed 42
python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --per_channel true --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm none --seed 42
```

eval-bot: job queued: eval-4287654321-1 (per_channel true, norm l2) — ETA ~8m. job queued: eval-4287654321-2 (per_channel true, norm none) — ETA ~9m.

devansh: also check whitening/centering. if training and production pipelines differ on mean-centering it's a classic top-1 shift. run a quick `--apply_whitening=false` vs true test.

morgan: added a 3rd job with whitening toggle:
```
python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --per_channel true --apply_whitening true --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm l2 --seed 42
```

anya: fwiw we had a shortvec variant earlier where microbatch kvcache trimming slightly changed normalization for short contexts — double-check the production inference pipeline for any extra L2-normalize calls.

morgan: noted. confirming prod pipeline uses explicit `normalize=True` after pooling.

eval-bot: eval-4287654321-1 finished: recall@1 0.63 (+7ppt vs previous int4), recall@10 0.85. eval-4287654321-2 finished: recall@1 0.57, recall@10 0.84. eval-4287654321-3 finished: recall@1 0.66, recall@10 0.85.

devansh: nice — per-channel + whitening seems to recover most of the gap. looks like quantization granularity + centering matters for the high-similarity tail.

anya: can you generate a small QC report (1-slide) comparing cosine CDFs for the three runs and the fp16 baseline? want to share with infra to consider changing default `per_channel=true` for shortvec family.

morgan: i'll produce the QC and push to the onboarding doc. plan: make per-channel quant the canary default for shortvec-7B, schedule canary A/B on Dedicated (10% traffic) and monitor recall@1 and latency.

ops-bot: canary job scheduled for 2026-04-02 15:30 UTC on dedicated cluster `rdw-ded-3` — route 10% traffic to int4-perchannel variant.

devansh: also add eval slice for queries < 8 tokens and for multi-turn prompts; short queries seem to be the vulnerable slice.

morgan: added slices and the QC link: https://redwood.internal/embeddings/onboard/shortvec-7B/int4-qc (will attach slides). assigning follow-ups: anya -> infra change request, devansh -> run multi-seed stress, jia -> sanity-check normalization in prod client. i'll own the QC + canary monitor.

anya: ack.

jia: ack, will look at client normalization.

morgan: thanks team. will update thread after canary metrics. :thumbsup:
